messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: REDWOOD-INCIDENT PAGER — region=eu-central-1 — elevated 5xx for /v1/generate. Spike started ~2026-03-15T02:05Z. Probable targets: ALB/ELB + Route53 latency. Paging on-call: @dan-oncall. Please ack and triage. (severity=P1)

dan-oncall: Acked. I'm up. quick check: scope? global or region-specific?

alice.m: Seeing 4.7% 5xx across hosted API, but eu-central-1 is 36% of errors. App logs show connection reset from upstream and "504 backend timeout" from ALB. Customers reporting timeouts.

ben.platform: Graphs: ALB target_503_count and TargetResponseTime look correlated. Route53 health check for api-eu failed several times. Could be cross-AZ networking or EC2 instance issues.

carla-sre: Running quick probes:
```
curl -I https://api.eu.redwood.example.com/v1/health -m 5 -s -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n"
aws elb describe-instance-health --load-balancer-name prod-eu-alb --region eu-central-1
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --metric-name HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count --namespace AWS/ApplicationELB --start-time 2026-03-15T01:50:00Z --end-time 2026-03-15T02:10:00Z --period 60 --statistics Sum
```

carla-sre: curl intermittently returns 502 or times out. ELB describe shows several targets in Unhealthy state in az-1.

eva-net: I'm seeing route53 trace showing increased TTL misses and some resolver timeouts from two major ISPs into eu-central-1. But most traffic is hitting ALB and failing at targetgroup. Might be a dual issue.

frank-sre: Checked EC2: a few instances show high OS-level iowait and dmesg has repeated EBS IO timeout lines on i-0abcde12345f. EBS metrics: VolumeQueueLength spiked. Suspect intermittent EBS degrade on a subset of hosts.

ops-bot: Created AWS support case 1234567890 for EBS io latency in eu-central-1. Case owner: AWS-ENG. ETA: immediate triage.

dan-oncall: Plan: 1) shift Route53 weight off eu-central-1 to eu-west-1 failover 2) mark affected targets OutOfService so ALB drains them 3) scale up healthy pool in eu-west-1 for capacity 4) continue AWS case. Who can take Route53 change?

ben.platform: I can do Route53 weight change. Will run playbook. Will also update the health-check to reduce false failovers back.

ben.platform: Executing:
```
# shift 80% traffic to eu-west-1, leave 20% to avoid global cold starts
aws route53 change-traffic-policy-instance --id tp-abcdef --region us-east-1 --cli-input-json '{"Comment":"emergency shift eu-central-1 -> eu-west-1","Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-central-1","Weight":20,"TTL":60}}]}'
```

ben.platform: Update: change submitted to Route53, propagation in progress (TTL=60). :hourglass_flowing_sand:

carla-sre: Marking 6 instances in targetgroup prod-eu-tg as OutOfService to force replacement and avoid serving bad IO. Command: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-central-1:12345:targetgroup/prod-eu-tg/abcd --targets Id=i-0abcde12345f`

frank-sre: Starting instance recoveries now. Also attaching new volumes as replacement for 2 affected hosts. Replication in progress.

alice.m: Telemetry shows 5xx rate dropping to 8% overall after the route shift, eu-central-1 5xx reduced to 12%. Customers still see errors intermittently for in-flight sessions.

dan-oncall: Good. Keep health checks gentle for next 15m. ops-bot, please throttle alerting noise (suppress duplicates).

ops-bot: Suppressing duplicate 5xx alerts for 10m for region eu-central-1.

carla-sre: AWS support confirmed EBS backend experiencing elevated latency on a specific EBS-fingerprint. They recommend instance replacement and volume snapshot + create new volume. AWS is collecting logs. Case 1234567890.

frank-sre: Snapshots started. ETA for new volumes ~7m. I'm bootstrapping replacement instances into ASG with new volumes, will attach to TG after health ok.

ben.platform: Route53 propagation shows ~70% traffic now to eu-west-1 within DNS caches. Observed request rate in eu-west-1 up but healthy. No new 5xx from eu-west-1.

alice.m: Notifying support and customers: drafting status for status.redwood.example.com — will include that we've shifted traffic and are replacing affected hosts, AWS engaged.

sales-tilt: Heads-up: a few paying customers pinged SRE for SLA impact. Need ETA on recovery for status page.

dan-oncall: ETA: partial mitigation in 15-20m (traffic shift + instance replacement), full verification after volumes replaced and metrics stable (~1h). I'll update status. Assigning primary P0 owner: @carla-sre; secondary: @frank-sre.

carla-sre: Handoff: I'm going offline for 20m for a quick maintenance window to validate volume snapshots and reattach. @frank-sre please monitor the ALB target health and customer errors while I'm on short break.

frank-sre: Acknowledged, monitoring CloudWatch and logs. If 5xx > 5% for more than 2 consecutive mins, I'll trigger rollback DNS to 90% eu-west-1 and open new incident if needed.

ops-bot: Status update posted to #incident-updates: "Mitigation: Traffic shifted to eu-west-1; replacing affected eu-central-1 instances; AWS engaged (case 1234567890)."

alice.m: Logs show some clients retried and succeeded after shift. We'll keep canary traffic to eu-central-1 to validate repairs.

dan-oncall: Good job team. Once carla back, we'll reconvene for RCA play and include timeline. For now, keep paging to critical-only.

incident-bot: Incident P1 still active — monitoring. If resolved, please post final update and close the thread.
